issues.description: The Course.addRating method parameter label is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template expect addRating(stars: Int) but the solution's Course implementation defines addRating(value: Int) while the solution's Client calls addRating(stars: 4). This mismatch between the method definition and its call will cause compilation errors and is likely to confuse students about the correct external parameter label to implement.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the external parameter label consistent across artifacts. Change the solution's Course method signature to match the problem/template: func addRating(stars: Int) { ... } (or, if you prefer a different external label, update all call sites and the template/problem to use that label). Ensuring the same external parameter name (stars) in the Course implementation and all callers will resolve the compilation/confusion issue.

issues.description: The parameter label for the Course.addRating method is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement explicitly documents and the template stub declares addRating(stars:), but the solution implementation declares addRating(value:). Additionally, the solution's Client calls addRating(stars:), which does not match the solution implementation's parameter name. This mismatch can confuse students comparing the template/problem to the reference solution (which uses a different parameter identifier) and may lead to uncertainty about the correct method signature to implement.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the parameter label consistent across all artifacts. Prefer the problem-stated form addRating(stars:) and update the solution implementation to use that label (e.g. change func addRating(value: Int) to func addRating(stars: Int)) and ensure all calls (Client) match. This keeps the template, problem description, and reference solution aligned and avoids student confusion.
